items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I didn't know Red Callender, but somebody had told me he was a good bass player, so I called him up, and he said he'd be glad to make it.

ctx.x: Had you met Red Callender and Teddy Edwards when you got out to the Coast?

Well, I knew Teddy from Detroit, because I saw him in Detroit. But I didn't know Red Callender, but somebody had told me he was a good bass player, so I called him up, and he said he'd be glad to make it. He put his hand in my pocket, you know, but he made it! So I said, "Okay"... He charged me a lot of money.
Who did you have playing piano?

items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: For instance, I just happened to be looking at a record with Howard McGhee on Black-and-White, called "Ood-I-Koo Bop."

ctx.x: We've been spending some time with some discographies, and you have discovered a lot of records that you forgot to name.

Yes. For instance, I just happened to be looking at a record with Howard McGhee on Black-and-White, called "Ood-I-Koo Bop." I didn't remember that. And another thing with Benny Goodman. I had forgotten I had done a record with him, "The World Is Waiting For the Sunrise." I didn't mention all that.
